Since \(BP\) and \(BQ\) are two trisectors of \(\angle B\), they split \(\angle B\) into three equal parts. Given  
\[
\angle QBP=14^\circ,
\]
we have
\[
\angle B=3\cdot 14^\circ=42^\circ.
\]

Now in \(\triangle ABC\),
\[
\angle C=180^\circ-\angle A-\angle B
=180^\circ-39^\circ-42^\circ=99^\circ.
\]

The trisectors of \(\angle C\) divide it into three equal parts, so each part is
\[
\frac{99^\circ}{3}=33^\circ.
\]
Since \(P\) lies on the trisector closer to side \(BC\), we have
\[
\angle BCP=33^\circ.
\]
Also, \(BP\) is the trisector closer to \(BC\), so
\[
\angle PBC=14^\circ.
\]

In \(\triangle BPC\),
\[
\angle BPC=180^\circ-\angle PBC-\angle BCP
=180^\circ-14^\circ-33^\circ=133^\circ.
\]

The answer is \(133^\circ\).
